# TFLM — TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers

Lets customer-supplied `.tflite` models run on the IPRO7 CPU.

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | https://github.com/tensorflow/tflite-micro |
| Tree generated by | `tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/project_generation/create_tflm_tree.py` |
| License | Apache-2.0 (see `LICENSE`) |

Regenerating the tree needs GNU make ≥ 3.82; macOS ships 3.81, so use
`/opt/homebrew/opt/make/libexec/gnubin` on `PATH`.

## TFLM does not drive the NPU — and does not need to

The NPU consumes an offline-compiled instruction stream (`.blai`), and TFLM has
no delegate mechanism, so TFLM models run on the CPU. That is not a conflict:
`iproai_npu_inference()` blocks on a FreeRTOS semaphore and yields the core
while the NPU computes, so a TFLM model and a `.blai` model genuinely run
concurrently. The achievable overlap is bounded by how much of the `.blai`
graph actually maps to the NPU — measure `NPU_on` before assuming it is high.

## Kernel backends

`CONFIG_TFLM_NMSIS_NN_KERNELS` (default y) swaps 14 reference kernels for the
NMSIS-NN backend in `tensorflow/lite/micro/kernels/nmsis_nn/`.

Measured on `apps/test/ipro_tflm_test` (hello_world int8, FULLY_CONNECTED only):

| backend | `.text` | P-ext instructions |
|---|---|---|
| reference | 121,884 | 0 |
| nmsis_nn | 137,356 | 527 |
| delta | **+15,472** | |

`data` and `bss` are identical between the two.

### The nmsis_nn backend is generated, not forked

`tools/cmsis_to_nmsis.py` rewrites TFLM's upstream `cmsis_nn` backend. All 46
CMSIS-NN APIs that backend calls have exact NMSIS-NN counterparts, so the
mapping is purely mechanical (`arm_`→`riscv_`, `cmsis_nn_`→`nmsis_nn_`,
`ARM_`→`RISCV_`). Re-run it after upgrading the vendored TFLM rather than
hand-patching; the script fails loudly if any identifier is left unconverted.

### `-DCMSIS_NN` is deliberate

TFLM's kernel headers gate on `#if defined(CMSIS_NN)` to decide whether an
optimized backend supplies `Register_*_INT4/8/16()` or the header should emit
inline fallbacks. In TFLM's vocabulary the macro means "an optimized backend is
present", not "the backend is CMSIS". It is added as an `INTERFACE` definition
because `micro_mutable_op_resolver.h` pulls those headers into app translation
units too — a mismatch there gives duplicate symbol definitions at link time.

## C++17

TFLM needs C++17 (`std::is_integral_v`, `make_unsigned_t`, `common_type_t`).
The SDK's global `-std=c++11` in `cmake/compiler_flags.cmake` is now
`-std=${IPRO_CXX_STD}`, which resolves to `c++17` when
`CONFIG_COMPONENTS_TFLM_ENABLE` is set and `c++11` otherwise, so no existing
component changes behaviour.
